questions.q: What are the two layers of Tableau's data model?
options: The dashboard layer and the worksheet layer
The extract layer and the live-connection layer
The reporting layer and the storage layer
The logical layer (logical tables connected by relationships) and the physical layer (physical tables combined by joins/unions inside a logical table)
questions.explain: Every Tableau data source is built from a logical layer (relationships between logical tables) sitting on top of a physical layer (joins/unions inside each logical table).

questions.q: Where do relationships live, and where do joins live?
options: Relationships and joins are the same thing, just different names
Relationships connect logical tables to each other on the logical layer; joins combine physical tables inside one logical table on the physical layer
Joins only exist in Tableau Prep, never in Tableau Desktop
Relationships live in the physical layer; joins live in the logical layer
questions.explain: The logical layer holds relationships between logical tables; double-clicking into a logical table opens its physical layer, where you build joins or unions.

questions.q: How do you open the physical layer for a given logical table?
options: It opens automatically the first time you add a filter
Double-click the logical table on the data source canvas
Right-click the worksheet tab and select Physical Layer
You can only view it from Tableau Server, not Desktop
questions.explain: Double-clicking a logical table on the logical layer canvas opens its physical layer — the traditional join canvas underneath it.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what problem did the old single-layer canvas cause that relationships were built to fix?
options: It couldn't connect to Excel files at all
It joined every table to every other table immediately, which could duplicate rows and generate wasteful queries even for worksheets that didn't need most of the tables
It didn't support any join types besides inner join
It required writing SQL by hand for every join
questions.explain: Before the two-layer model, every table was joined at query time regardless of what a given worksheet needed, which could multiply rows and waste query performance — relationships are context-aware and avoid both problems.

options: A table that has no fields, only calculated fields
A table that only exists conceptually and can never be queried
A box on the logical layer canvas that may represent exactly one physical table, or several physical tables already joined or unioned together
Another name for a Tableau worksheet
questions.explain: A logical table is what you see on the main data source canvas — it can bundle one or many physical tables underneath it via the physical layer.
